typical_topologies: Shared address buses and multiple data buses (most common — address-channel bandwidth is significantly less than data-channel bandwidth)
Multilayer, with multiple address and data buses

interconnect_role.definition: An interconnect between devices is equivalent to another device with symmetrical master and slave ports, so that real master/slave devices can be connected to it.
interconnect_role.register_slices: Each AXI channel transfers information in only one direction, with no fixed relationship between channels. A register slice can be inserted at almost any point in any channel, at the cost of one additional cycle of latency. This trades latency for maximum operating frequency.

interconnect_rules: Interconnect must realign the address and write data when determining the destination address space or slave space, so that write data is signaled as valid only to the slave it is destined for.

When a master is connected to an interconnect, the interconnect appends additional bits to the ARID, AWID and WID identifiers that are unique to that master port. Effects: (a) masters do not need to know what ID values other masters use; (b) ID identifier at the slave interface is wider than at the master interface.

For read data, the interconnect uses the additional bits of the RID identifier to determine which master port the read data is destined for, then removes these bits before passing RID to the master port.

For write response, the interconnect uses the additional bits of the BID identifier to determine which master port the response is destined for, then removes these bits before passing BID to the master port.
The interconnect must ensure that read data from a sequence of transactions with the same ARID targeting different slaves is received by the master in the order it issued the addresses.
An interconnect that combines write transactions from different masters must forward the write data in address order.
If the interconnect cannot successfully decode a slave access, it must return the DECERR response. Recommendation: route to a default slave that returns DECERR.
An AXI4 interconnect must preserve same-ID-same-slave ordering for Device (Non-modifiable) transactions; this is not an explicit requirement of AXI3.

AXI4 interconnect may convert INCR bursts with length >16 into multiple smaller bursts even if Non-modifiable. Generated bursts must retain the same transaction characteristics; only burst length is reduced and address adapted.

For locked transactions (AXI3 only), the interconnect must ensure that only the originating master can access the targeted slave region until an unlocked transaction from the same master completes; an arbiter within the interconnect must enforce this restriction.

In an AXI4 environment, the interconnect must convert any AXI3 locked transaction (AxLOCK[1:0]=0b10) into a normal transaction (AxLOCK=0b0); the conversion mechanism should optionally detect and flag that translation occurred.
Non-modifiable transaction parameters (AxADDR, AxSIZE, AxLEN, AxBURST, AxLOCK, AxCACHE, AxPROT) must not be changed by the interconnect when AxCACHE Modifiable bit is deasserted.
Each AXI interface has a single clock signal ACLK; an interconnect may include synchronous or asynchronous bridges between clock domains, but each interface itself is single-clock.
ARESETn may be asserted asynchronously, but deassertion must be synchronous with a rising edge of ACLK.
Interconnect must not introduce combinational paths from any READY signal back to the corresponding VALID signal.
The interconnect (when transforming Non-modifiable AXI4 INCR>16 into multiple smaller bursts) must generate bursts whose length is <=16 and whose start addresses are appropriately adapted.

id_routing.description: Slave-side ID_WIDTH > master-side ID_WIDTH. The interconnect appends additional bits to ARID/AWID/WID at each master port; these bits encode the originating master port. On the return path (RID, BID) the interconnect uses those bits to route the response, then strips them before delivering RID/BID to the destination master.
id_routing.implication: A slave-port ID_WIDTH parameter must accommodate the maximum of (master-port ID_WIDTH + ceil(log2(num_master_ports))).

guaranteed: Transaction requests on the same channel with the same ID and destination remain in order.
Transaction responses with the same ID are returned in request-issue order.
Read data for transactions with the same ARID (even targeting different slaves) is delivered in address-issue order to the master.
not_guaranteed: Ordering between transactions from different masters
Ordering between read and write transactions
Ordering between transactions with different IDs
Ordering between transactions to different Peripheral regions
Ordering between transactions to different Memory locations
ordering_guarantees.device_ordering_axi4_only: AXI4: All Device (Non-modifiable) transactions using the same ID to the same slave must be ordered with respect to each other (NOT required in AXI3).

multi_copy_atomicity.required_for: Issue G and later of this specification (also required if Arm v8 architecture processors are used).
multi_copy_atomicity.english: A system is multi-copy atomic iff (a) writes to the same location are observed in the same order by all agents AND (b) a write to a location that is observable by one agent is observable by all agents.
implementation_options: Use a single Point of Serialization for each address, ensuring all accesses to the same location are ordered AND that all coherent cached copies are invalidated before the new value becomes visible to any agent.
Avoid the use of forwarding buffers upstream of any agent, which would otherwise allow a buffered write to become visible to some agents before all agents.

memory_vs_peripheral_regions.Memory_location: Read returns last value written; write updates value retrievable by subsequent read; accesses have no side-effects on other Memory locations; size = single-copy atomicity size.
memory_vs_peripheral_regions.Peripheral_region: Read may not return last value written; write may not update value retrievable by subsequent read; accesses may have side-effects on other addresses within the region; size is IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED but must be contained within a single slave.

slave_classification.Memory_slave: Required to handle all transaction types correctly. Memory slaves use Table A9-2/A9-4 default signal value rules.
slave_classification.Peripheral_slave: Has an IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED method of access. Any non-conforming access must complete protocol-compliantly but the peripheral is not required to operate correctly afterward.

evidence.spec_section: A1.2.2 Interface and interconnect / Typical system topologies
evidence.quote: Most systems use one of three interconnect topologies: shared address and data buses; shared address buses and multiple data buses; multilayer, with multiple address and data buses. In most systems, the address channel bandwidth requirement is significantly less than the data channel bandwidth requirement.

Each AXI channel transfers information in only one direction, and the architecture does not require any fixed relationship between the channels. A register slice can be inserted at almost any point in any channel, at the cost of an additional cycle of latency.

evidence.spec_section: A5.2.3 Interconnect use of transaction identifiers
evidence.quote: When a master is connected to an interconnect, the interconnect appends additional bits to the ARID, AWID and WID identifiers that are unique to that master port. The ID identifier at a slave interface is wider than the ID identifier at a master interface. For read data, the interconnect uses the additional bits of the RID identifier to determine which master port the read data is destined for. The interconnect removes these bits of the RID identifier before passing the RID value to the correct master port.

The interconnect must ensure that the read data from a sequence of transactions with the same ARID value targeting different slaves is received by the master in the order that it issued the addresses.
An interconnect that combines write transactions from different masters must ensure that it forwards the write data in address order.

If the interconnect cannot successfully decode a slave access, it must return the DECERR response. This specification recommends that the interconnect routes the access to a default slave, and the default slave returns the DECERR response.

AWID default All zeros; AWLEN All zeros, Length 1; AWSIZE Data bus width; AWBURST 0b01 INCR; AWLOCK All zeros Normal access; AWCACHE 0b0000; AWQOS 0b0000; WSTRB All ones; BRESP 0b00 OKAY (slave-side default). ARID, ARLEN, ARSIZE, ARBURST, ARLOCK, ARCACHE, ARQOS all have the same defaults as their AW counterparts.

When a master uses the AxLOCK signals for a transaction to show that it is a locked transaction then the interconnect must ensure that only that master can access the targeted slave region, until an unlocked transaction from the same master completes. An arbiter within the interconnect must enforce this restriction.
In an AXI4 environment, any AXI3 locked transaction is converted as follows: AWLOCK[1:0] = 0b10 -> AWLOCK = 0b0; ARLOCK[1:0] = 0b10 -> ARLOCK = 0b0.
In AXI4, all Device transactions using the same ID to the same slave must be ordered with respect to each other. This ordering is not an explicit requirement of AXI3.

evidence.spec_section: A4.3 AXI4 changes — Non-modifiable / burst splitting
evidence.quote: AXI4 INCR bursts of length >16 can be converted to multiple smaller bursts even if Non-modifiable. The generated bursts must retain the same transaction characteristics, except the burst length is reduced and the address is adapted appropriately.
It is required that the Multi_Copy_Atomicity property is True for Issue G and later of this specification.

Transaction requests on the same channel, with the same ID and destination are guaranteed to remain in order. The ordering model does not give any ordering guarantees between transactions from different masters, read and write transactions, transactions with different IDs, transactions to different Peripheral regions, or transactions to different Memory locations.

evidence.spec_section: A6.2 Memory locations and Peripheral regions
evidence.quote: A Memory location has all of the following properties: a read of a byte returns the last value written; write updates value; accesses have no side-effects on other Memory locations; size = single-copy atomicity size. A Peripheral region has all of: read does not necessarily return last value written; write does not necessarily update; accesses may have side-effects on other addresses within the region; size is IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED but must be contained within a single slave component.
